questions.q: Most Payables setup in Oracle Fusion is scoped at which level?
options: A single global switch for the entire deployment
questions.explain: Payables setup, such as tolerances and default payment terms, is mostly scoped per business unit, which is why two BUs can behave differently.

questions.q: Why can two business units within the same company run Payables with different invoice tolerances?
options: They can't — tolerances are always company-wide
Because tolerances depend only on the supplier's country
Because tolerances are set per individual employee
Because tolerances and many other Payables settings are configured per business unit
questions.explain: Payables Options, including tolerances, are set at the business unit level, so BUs can legitimately differ.

questions.q: An invoice is stuck with no due date calculated. Which setup area should you check first?
questions.explain: Payment terms are the rules that calculate an invoice's due date and any discount, so a missing due date points there first.

questions.q: Which of the seven setup areas determines the chart of accounts and currency behind a posted invoice?
questions.explain: The business unit is tied to a primary ledger, which drives the chart of accounts and currency rules for everything it posts.

questions.q: A brand-new supplier cannot be paid yet even though their invoice validated and was approved. Which area most likely needs attention?
options: The supplier's record, such as a missing bank account
questions.explain: Payment typically requires a complete supplier record, including a valid bank account for electronic payment methods.
